$schema_notes: Registry of published claude.ai Artifacts whose source lives in THIS repo.
Purpose: a published artifact keeps its URL only if a later session passes that URL back to
the Artifact tool. Without a durable record, a new session mints a NEW url and the old link
goes stale. Prose in a handoff is not enough - this file is the machine-readable anchor.
TO REFRESH AN ARTIFACT (any session, no prior context needed):
1. WebFetch the `url` FIRST. The Artifact tool refuses to redeploy from a session that has
not viewed the live version ('This session hasn't viewed the latest version'). It is also
how you detect that another session republished without committing its source.
2. Bring the page current, according to `content_model`:
narrative-snapshot - the `source` file IS the page. Edit it.
generated          - `source` is a GENERATOR, usually not even HTML. Run `render` to
produce `publish_from`. Fix wrong output in the generator or in the
DATA it reads, NEVER in the rendered HTML - the next render discards
edits to it silently.
3. Call the Artifact tool with BOTH `url` (from this file) and `file_path` = `source` for a
narrative-snapshot, or `publish_from` for a generated entry. Passing `url` is what
redeploys in place. Omitting it mints a new URL - do not omit it.
4. Reuse the recorded `favicon` verbatim. A changed favicon reads as a different page.
5. Update `last_published` here in the same commit as the source edit.
`session` SCOPES WHICH HANDOFFS CONSIDER THIS PAGE. A session name means only that
workstream's handoffs refresh it; `"*"` means EVERY handoff must consider it, which is what a
cross-track status page needs. Scope it to what the page REPORTS ON, not to who maintains it -
the lane board sat 3 days stale because it was scoped to one track while reporting on eight.
The `title` lives in the source file's <title> tag, not here - here it is a mirror for humans.
Titles must NOT carry a hard date: these are living pages, the as-of stamp belongs in the body.

artifacts.description: Live lane board generated from agentic_os.lane: 32 lanes across 8 tracks, who holds what right now, and the reconciliation query behind every number.

RECONCILED.decided_by: Dave, asked directly -- this was a decision, not a bug, and the prior session correctly refused to guess it
RECONCILED.what_was_wrong: This entry described a hand-authored 51KB narrative snapshot while the URL served a ~100KB render-board.mjs output. Found 2026-07-29 by session 08e4b3c5, which WebFetched the live page before trusting the registry and then deliberately published nothing.
RECONCILED.resolution: The board IS a generated live board. source/content_model/description/session now match what is actually published, and the 2026-07-26 decision below is marked SUPERSEDED rather than deleted.
closed_before_publishing: render-board.mjs held counter: was `open.filter((l) => l.owner_session_id).length` in JS, which never read lease_expires_at, so the headline counted ABANDONED lanes as held and contradicted its own 'lease lapsed' rows. Now a SQL `held_now` column that is the exact complement of lane.mjs's RECLAIMABLE (both an expired lease AND a quiet holder). Verified against psql: of 3 owned open lanes, exactly 1 is genuinely held; the old code would have said 3. Headline, filter chip and rendered rows all agree at 1.
The lane rows' `data-held` and `is-held` now use held_now too -- otherwise the fixed headline would have disagreed with the rows the 'held' FILTER shows, trading one contradiction for another.

The two reconciliation queries the page PRINTS were wrong in a way that mattered more than the counter: the sessions query advertised bare `last_heartbeat > now()` while the code had already been fixed to GREATEST(...). The page's whole affordance is that any figure can be falsified in ten seconds, so a printed query that misstates the predicate is a lie with a verification badge on it.

Stale aos-data-hardening lane note ('dev server on 3010 pid 34904', 'Releasing this lane unowned') fixed IN THE DATABASE via lane.mjs note. Notes render verbatim, so an HTML edit would have been discarded by the next render.
RECONCILED.guard_ratcheted: liveness-predicate-guard.mjs minCorrect for render-board.mjs raised 4 -> 9, set to the MEASURED count. A first attempt at 6 PASSED the negative control -- deleting held_now left 8, still above the floor -- i.e. the ratchet would have shipped without protecting the thing it was added for. That guard now also detects HTML-ESCAPED bare-heartbeat tests (`>` instead of `>`), which is why the printed query's regression had been invisible to it all along.
RECONCILED.structural_fix: create_handoff SKILL.md now (a) supports `session: "*"` so a cross-track page is considered by EVERY handoff, and (b) handles `content_model: generated` -- run `render`, publish `publish_from`, never hand the generator to the Artifact tool. Without both, the decisions above would have been recorded in a file nothing honors: the wildcard was chosen precisely because the old match-on-session-name rule is why no handoff ever looked at this page.
